## What I did

Downloaded **1BTL** from RCSB and verified it before designing anything:

- Chain A, 263 residues, Ambler numbering 26–290 (gaps at 239/253, the standard class A convention)
- Ser70, Lys73, Ser130, Asp131, Asn132, Glu166, Asn170, Lys234, Ser235, Ala237, Arg244 all present at expected identities
- Native **Cys77–Cys123** disulfide intact (SG–SG 2.01 Å)
- vs. UniProt **P62593**: only 2 differences, Ambler **84 (V→I)** and **184 (A→V)**. Note: A184V is itself one of the known stabilizing global suppressors — your construct already has it.

**Exclusion zone** (your constraint, enforced computationally): the catalytic set {70, 73, 130, 131, 132, 166, 170, 234, 235, 236, 237, 244} + everything within 10 Å of the catalytic functional groups (Ser70 OG, Lys73 NZ, Ser130 OG, Glu166 OE1/OE2, Lys234 NZ, Ser235 OG) + the Ω-loop (161–179) + the native Cys pair. That removed **82 of 263 positions**, leaving 181 designable. Ser70 is untouched in every proposal below.

**Tools/methods run** (all in the Python REPL): freesasa relative SASA (Tien 2013 max-ASA reference); pydssp secondary structure; grid void detection (0.5 Å grid, 1.1 Å probe, bulk solvent component removed → **166.1 Å³ total internal void**); per-residue packing density and adjacent void volume; Cβ–Cβ / Cα–Cα / pseudo-χ3 disulfide geometry scan; backbone-NH H-bond census for proline siting; φ/ψ for all residues; and **ESM-1v (`esm1v_t33_650M_UR90S_1`) masked-marginal scoring of all 4,997 single substitutions**. Literature via PubMed.

Sanity check on the ESM run: Ser70 substitutions score **−12.3 to −14.2**, among the most negative in the protein — the model independently flags the catalytic serine as untouchable.

## Tier 1 — recommended

| Mutation | ESM-1v | RSA | B (Ų) | d(Ser70) | Nearest catalytic | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **M182T** | **+6.76** | 17% | 5.6 | 13.1 Å | Arg244, 11.7 Å | Highest-scoring substitution of all 4,997; experimentally validated |
| **T265M** | +2.44 | 2.7% | 6.1 | 10.7 Å | Arg244, 3.1 Å (backbone only) | Most under-packed buried site; experimentally validated |
| **L201P** | +3.07 | 62% | 15.9 | 21.1 Å | Lys73, 16.4 Å | Ideal helix-N1 proline site (my prediction) |

**M182T** — the single highest masked-marginal score anywhere outside the exclusion zone. Experimentally established as a thermostabilizing "global suppressor": Huang & Palzkill, *PNAS* (*A natural polymorphism in beta-lactamase is a global suppressor*); Brown et al., *J Mol Biol*; Marciano et al., *Biochemistry*; Orencia et al., *Nat Struct Biol* (TEM-52 structure, M182T 17 Å from the active site). Mechanism attributed to stabilizing a helix at the α/β domain interface (Markov-state-model study, *ACS Cent Sci*). M182S is the alternative (ESM +4.90); a saturation-mutagenesis study of position 182 (*Int J Mol Sci*) found Tm varies strongly and multidirectionally with the identity at 182, so T is the safe pick.

**T265M** — Thr265 is the **most under-packed buried designable position** (34.6 Å³ of adjacent internal void at RSA 2.7%) and lines the protein's **largest internal cavity** (7.9 Å³ water-accessible, lined by Ala36/Leu40/Val44/Ile263/Tyr264/Thr265/Arg275/Gln278/Ile279/Ile282). Met adds ~47 Å³ into that void. Experimentally confirmed to raise TEM-1 thermal stability (Brown, Shaw, Palzkill et al., *J Mol Biol*, *Multiple global suppressors of protein stability defects…*). Two caveats I measured: Thr265 OG1 donates an H-bond to Arg43 backbone O (2.81 Å) that Met loses; and Thr265 is the β-strand partner of **Arg244** via backbone H-bonds (N–O 3.11 Å, O–N 3.16 Å). The *backbone* is unchanged and the side chain does not reach the Arg244 guanidinium (Thr265 CG2 → Arg244 CB, 4.04 Å), so Arg244 stays anchored — but this is the one proposal in physical contact with a catalytic residue. ESM prefers T265L (+5.13); I recommend M because that's the variant with Tm data.

**L201P** — the only high-quality proline site in the whole protein. Leu201 is the **N1 residue of helix H9** (Thr200 is loop, Leu201 begins the helix), φ = −56°, ψ = −43° (ideal for Pro), and its backbone NH donates **no** H-bond (nearest acceptor 3.88 Å) — the usual disqualifier for Pro engineering. Exposed (RSA 62%), flexible (B = 15.9), 21 Å from Ser70. Stabilizes by restricting unfolded-state backbone entropy. **This is a prediction, not a lookup** — I found no Tm measurement for L201P.

## Tier 2 — plausible, lower confidence

| Mutation | ESM-1v | Adjacent void | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| A224V | −1.93 | 16.1 Å³ | Fills 2nd cavity (Leu221/Arg222/Ala224/Leu225/Ile231/Leu250/Gly283/Ala284/Leu286/Ile287); RSA 21% so methyls can relax outward. ESM disagrees. |
| A36L / A36I | +2.52 / +1.96 | 19.0 Å³ | Buried (RSA 0.7%), lines cavity 1. **Do not combine with T265M** without repacking — same cavity. |
| V44I | +0.16 | 28.0 Å³ | Conservative +1 methyl core fill |
| V261I | +0.04 | 18.9 Å³ | Conservative +1 methyl core fill |
| Q278V/L/I | +5.50/+5.28/+4.57 | 20.1 Å³ | High model score, but structurally uncertain: the amide is H-bonded into a Gln39/Lys32 network and there is **zero** void at the amide tip |

## Checked and rejected — with reasons

- **No unsatisfied buried charges exist.** All 10 buried charged residues (Lys32, Glu37, Glu48, Glu58, Glu89, Asp157, Arg204, Arg259, Arg275, Gln278) are fully H-bonded or salt-bridged. That whole avenue is closed.
- **Glycine→Ala is mostly unavailable.** 13 of 17 designable glycines have **φ > 0** (left-handed) and are conformationally required. Only Gly78 and Gly283 have α-helical φ/ψ. **G283A rejected**: its virtual Cβ sits 2.76 Å from Leu221 CD2 — a clash needing Leu221 repacking (likely why Gly283 is conserved). Gly78 is in the helix bearing Cys77 of the native disulfide, with only 7.5 Å³ of adjacent void.
- **Second engineered disulfide rejected.** Best geometric pair is **A42C/S268C** (Cβ–Cβ 3.99 Å, Cα–Cα 5.14 Å, pseudo-χ3 −95°, 226 residues apart, 16.9 Å from the active site) — textbook geometry. But Ser268 OG caps a turn with three H-bonds (Leu40 O 2.82, Gln269 N 3.12, Ala270 N 3.02 Å), ESM is strongly against both (A42C −7.75, S268C −10.73), and there's mis-pairing risk with the existing Cys77–Cys123 pair. H26C/H289C (termini staple, 263 residues apart) is low-risk but likely low-reward.
- **F230K/F230R** scored +5.85/+5.39 — rejected: Phe230 is buried (RSA 11.4%), so these bury a charge. A clean illustration that ESM-1v is a fitness/conservation model, **not** a ΔΔG predictor.
- **R275Q and N276D are experimentally validated TEM-1 thermostabilizers** (same Brown et al. paper) but I excluded both under your constraint: Asn276 OD1 H-bonds **Arg244** NE (3.04 Å) and NH2 (3.25 Å) directly, and Arg275 Cβ is 4.53 Å from Arg244 Cβ. Both are known inhibitor-resistance determinants acting through Arg244 — they would change catalysis and inhibitor binding. Your call if you want to relax the constraint; they're the next-best validated options.
- **A184V**, a third validated suppressor, is **already present** in 1BTL.
- Surface electrostatics: 35 exposed charge-unpaired residues found (e.g. Glu110/Lys111 8.0 Å apart on one helix face), but expected gains are ~0.1–0.5 kcal/mol each and I did not model them. Low priority.

## Limitations — read before ordering primers

I had **no ΔΔG predictor** in this session (no FoldX, Rosetta, or PyRosetta) and ran no MD. **I did not compute a ΔΔG or ΔTm for any mutation.** The ESM-1v numbers are unitless evolutionary log-odds, and part of M182T's exceptional score reflects that it is a *frequent natural TEM variant* (its prevalence has nearly doubled per the saturation-mutagenesis paper) — the model is partly reading variant frequency, not thermodynamics. All stability claims for M182T, T265M, R275Q, N276D and A184V come from the cited experimental literature. Everything geometric (RSA, void volumes, φ/ψ, H-bonds, disulfide geometry, packing) is my own calculation on 1BTL and is reported as measured.

Suggested build: **M182T** alone first, then **M182T + T265M**, then add **L201P**. The Brown et al. work shows these suppressors act additively on stability. Assay Tm by DSF or CD and confirm kcat/KM on nitrocefin — Ala237/Arg244/Ser70 are untouched, so activity should be retained, but T265M's contact with the Arg244 strand makes that check non-optional.

## ANSWER

**Tier 1 (recommended, Ser70 and all catalytic residues untouched):**
- **M182T** — ESM-1v masked-marginal **+6.76** (highest of 4,997 single mutants outside the active site); 13.1 Å from Ser70; experimentally validated thermostabilizer (Huang & Palzkill *PNAS*; Brown et al. *JMB*; Orencia et al. *Nat Struct Biol*)
- **T265M** — most under-packed buried designable position (34.6 Å³ adjacent void, RSA 2.7%), fills 1BTL's largest internal cavity; ESM +2.44; experimentally validated (Brown et al. *JMB*)
- **L201P** — helix-H9 N1 position, φ/ψ = −56°/−43°, backbone NH free (3.88 Å); ESM +3.07; **my prediction, no Tm data**

**Tier 2:** A224V, A36L/A36I, V44I, V261I, Q278V (do not combine A36 with T265M — same cavity)

**Build order:** M182T → M182T+T265M → +L201P. Confirm Tm by DSF/CD and kcat/KM on nitrocefin.

**Not computed:** no ΔΔG or ΔTm — no FoldX/Rosetta/MD tool was available. ESM-1v scores are unitless fitness log-odds, not thermodynamics; all stability magnitudes are from the cited literature.

**Excluded despite being validated stabilizers:** R275Q and N276D (both directly contact catalytic Arg244 — Asn276 OD1–Arg244 NE 3.04 Å); A184V is already present in 1BTL.

**M182T** — the single highest masked-marginal score anywhere outside the exclusion zone. Experimentally established as a thermostabilizing "global suppressor": Huang & Palzkill, *PNAS* (*A natural polymorphism in beta-lactamase is a global suppressor*); Brown et al., *J Mol Biol*; Marciano et al., *Biochemistry*; Orencia et al., *Nat Struct Biol* (TEM-52 structure, M182T 17 Å from the active site). Mechanism attributed to stabilizing a helix at the α/β domain interface (Markov-state-model study, *ACS Cent Sci*). M182S is the alternative (ESM +4.90); a saturation-mutagenesis study of position 182 (*Int J Mol Sci*) found Tm varies strongly and multidirectionally with the identity at 182, so T is the safe pick.

**T265M** — Thr265 is the **most under-packed buried designable position** (34.6 Å³ of adjacent internal void at RSA 2.7%) and lines the protein's **largest internal cavity** (7.9 Å³ water-accessible, lined by Ala36/Leu40/Val44/Ile263/Tyr264/Thr265/Arg275/Gln278/Ile279/Ile282). Met adds ~47 Å³ into that void. Experimentally confirmed to raise TEM-1 thermal stability (Brown, Shaw, Palzkill et al., *J Mol Biol*, *Multiple global suppressors of protein stability defects…*). Two caveats I measured: Thr265 OG1 donates an H-bond to Arg43 backbone O (2.81 Å) that Met loses; and Thr265 is the β-strand partner of **Arg244** via backbone H-bonds (N–O 3.11 Å, O–N 3.16 Å). The *backbone* is unchanged and the side chain does not reach the Arg244 guanidinium (Thr265 CG2 → Arg244 CB, 4.04 Å), so Arg244 stays anchored — but this is the one proposal in physical contact with a catalytic residue. ESM prefers T265L (+5.13); I recommend M because that's the variant with Tm data.

**L201P** — the only high-quality proline site in the whole protein. Leu201 is the **N1 residue of helix H9** (Thr200 is loop, Leu201 begins the helix), φ = −56°, ψ = −43° (ideal for Pro), and its backbone NH donates **no** H-bond (nearest acceptor 3.88 Å) — the usual disqualifier for Pro engineering. Exposed (RSA 62%), flexible (B = 15.9), 21 Å from Ser70. Stabilizes by restricting unfolded-state backbone entropy. **This is a prediction, not a lookup** — I found no Tm measurement for L201P.

## Checked and rejected — with reasons

- **No unsatisfied buried charges exist.** All 10 buried charged residues (Lys32, Glu37, Glu48, Glu58, Glu89, Asp157, Arg204, Arg259, Arg275, Gln278) are fully H-bonded or salt-bridged. That whole avenue is closed.
- **Glycine→Ala is mostly unavailable.** 13 of 17 designable glycines have **φ > 0** (left-handed) and are conformationally required. Only Gly78 and Gly283 have α-helical φ/ψ. **G283A rejected**: its virtual Cβ sits 2.76 Å from Leu221 CD2 — a clash needing Leu221 repacking (likely why Gly283 is conserved). Gly78 is in the helix bearing Cys77 of the native disulfide, with only 7.5 Å³ of adjacent void.
- **Second engineered disulfide rejected.** Best geometric pair is **A42C/S268C** (Cβ–Cβ 3.99 Å, Cα–Cα 5.14 Å, pseudo-χ3 −95°, 226 residues apart, 16.9 Å from the active site) — textbook geometry. But Ser268 OG caps a turn with three H-bonds (Leu40 O 2.82, Gln269 N 3.12, Ala270 N 3.02 Å), ESM is strongly against both (A42C −7.75, S268C −10.73), and there's mis-pairing risk with the existing Cys77–Cys123 pair. H26C/H289C (termini staple, 263 residues apart) is low-risk but likely low-reward.
- **F230K/F230R** scored +5.85/+5.39 — rejected: Phe230 is buried (RSA 11.4%), so these bury a charge. A clean illustration that ESM-1v is a fitness/conservation model, **not** a ΔΔG predictor.
- **R275Q and N276D are experimentally validated TEM-1 thermostabilizers** (same Brown et al. paper) but I excluded both under your constraint: Asn276 OD1 H-bonds **Arg244** NE (3.04 Å) and NH2 (3.25 Å) directly, and Arg275 Cβ is 4.53 Å from Arg244 Cβ. Both are known inhibitor-resistance determinants acting through Arg244 — they would change catalysis and inhibitor binding. Your call if you want to relax the constraint; they're the next-best validated options.
- **A184V**, a third validated suppressor, is **already present** in 1BTL.
- Surface electrostatics: 35 exposed charge-unpaired residues found (e.g. Glu110/Lys111 8.0 Å apart on one helix face), but expected gains are ~0.1–0.5 kcal/mol each and I did not model them. Low priority.

## Limitations — read before ordering primers

I had **no ΔΔG predictor** in this session (no FoldX, Rosetta, or PyRosetta) and ran no MD. **I did not compute a ΔΔG or ΔTm for any mutation.** The ESM-1v numbers are unitless evolutionary log-odds, and part of M182T's exceptional score reflects that it is a *frequent natural TEM variant* (its prevalence has nearly doubled per the saturation-mutagenesis paper) — the model is partly reading variant frequency, not thermodynamics. All stability claims for M182T, T265M, R275Q, N276D and A184V come from the cited experimental literature. Everything geometric (RSA, void volumes, φ/ψ, H-bonds, disulfide geometry, packing) is my own calculation on 1BTL and is reported as measured.

Suggested build: **M182T** alone first, then **M182T + T265M**, then add **L201P**. The Brown et al. work shows these suppressors act additively on stability. Assay Tm by DSF or CD and confirm kcat/KM on nitrocefin — Ala237/Arg244/Ser70 are untouched, so activity should be retained, but T265M's contact with the Arg244 strand makes that check non-optional.
